heroHeadline: Heaviest Baidoa Clashes Yet Wound 71, Kill One as Laftagareen Militia Storms Southwest State Capital
heroSubtitle: Fighting erupted before dawn on September 3, 2026 in Baidoa between federal government forces and Darawish militia loyal to former Southwest State president Laftagareen — the most serious clash in the city since the August 17 VBIED assault — with Laftagareen's forces seizing the Ninth Brigade base and several neighbourhoods before the shooting subsided by early afternoon. Somalia's Defense Ministry said Al-Shabaab fought alongside the militia, a claim Laftagareen's spokesman publicly denied while claiming sole responsibility for the operation; Ethiopian AUSSOM troops holding the airport and presidential compound took no part in the fighting. Bay Regional Hospital reported 71 wounded, including 15 women, and one civilian killed — the clearest casualty toll yet for the five-month Southwest State standoff. The clash lands atop an accelerating UN drawdown: UNSOS has moved into asset liquidation and staff layoffs as roughly 11,862 uniformed AUSSOM personnel remain dependent on its logistics chain ahead of the US funding cutoff at year-end, while Egyptian troop reinforcements meant to backfill the mission have themselves been delayed by funding and logistical hurdles.
